prediction.likelyOutcome: Quantum is the favorite to collect most or all of the $24,179.35 unpaid balance at trial: the payment history, substantial-performance posture, and the parties' own agreed remedial fix at the November 12 meeting undercut Plaza de Kaza's defect counterclaim, though Hula's standard-of-care criticism and the unresolved agency question (Dykstra vs. Plaza de Kaza as obligor) create real, if secondary, litigation risk. Because Plaza de Kaza has put no repair-cost or diminution figure into this record, any setoff a factfinder awards is more likely to be modest than to wipe out the claim.

issues.label: Breach of Contract — Unpaid Final Invoice

figures.label: unpaid final invoice balance
figures.quote: Darehshori, however, stated that he refused to pay the remaining $24,179.35 balance because Quantum did not correctly pour the traffic circle and not because he was angry with Trimberger.

issues.label: Agency — Dykstra vs. Plaza de Kaza as True Obligor

outcome.description: After a three-day bench trial the court found Dykstra breached his agreement with Quantum and Plaza de Kaza was unjustly enriched, and entered judgment against both for $24,179.35 (the full final invoice, no setoffs), rejecting Plaza de Kaza's counterclaims; Quantum's later motion for attorney-fee sanctions was denied. The Court of Appeals affirmed (Quantum's challenges to the lien dismissal and the sanctions ruling failed).
